notes.title: Devblog #1: Identity Crisis
notes.notes:
[p][i]Phew! [/i]These past few days were awesome, ProtonVR was first publicly displayed to the world and the feedback was [b]great. [/b][/p][p][/p][p]Welcome to the first [b]Dev Blog[/b] where I will post up-to date information regarding the state of ProtonVR's development. Let's take a look at what happened so far.[/p][h2]Reception & Feedback[/h2][p]One of the biggest feedbacks from the internet was [url="https://www.reddit.com/r/virtualreality/comments/1modq26/my_first_game_is_a_cool_little_vr_retro_shooter/"]on Reddit[/url].
I want to reach out to all those who sent kind words of encouragement and excitement for the game, it's awesome to see people excited for something I'm putting so much care to. [i]Thank you.[/i][/p][p]Your input is most valuable and a lot of people joined the [b]discord[/b] and are actively making cool suggestions and the dialog for smart-decision making is happening![/p][p]But there is something in the comments that sticks out like a sore thumb...[/p][h2]Comparisons with [url="https://store.steampowered.com/app/615120/compound"]COMPOUND[/url][/h2][p]As I've been forward about it many times, ProtonVR takes inspiration from COMPOUND, that is true, always has been and always will. [i]I am a big fan of the game![/i][/p][p][/p][p]As one Reddit user so [i]kindly[/i] put it:[/p][p][i][u]"bro just took Compound and slightly changed it. It’s almost identical."[/u][/i][/p][p][i]-Anonymous[/i][/p][p]
As noted by the community the similarities are [b]strong[/b], so what gives?[/p][p]Some see this as a positive, [b]albeit a [i]significant part is sceptical[/i][/b], and [b]rightfully so![/b] I am, and always will, be a [b]Player[/b], before I am a developer, and [b]I couldn't agree more with you[/b]. [/p][p][i]Note: Since the very early development of this game, I've been in constant contact with [b]Bevan McKechnie,[/b] the developer of COMPOUND, and I received more than my share of encouragement and support one could ask from someone I hold in high professional regard. His artistic work has given me [b]valuable lessons[/b] in improving my own Pixel Art.[/i][/p][p]But the truth if it is:[/p][h3][b][i]I was inspired by [/i][/b][i]COMPOUND [b]but I want ProtonVR[/b] [b]to have it's own Identity![/b][/i][/h3][p]Comparisons are always bound to happen, but [i]I am not content with the intensity it did[/i][b]. [/b][i]It exceeded flattery [/i]and [i]it made me feel creatively dishonest[/i], which is why some changes are going to happen to ProtonVR.[/p][p]ProtonVR will go through some changes to set itself further apart from any other game out there, but there [b]are things [/b]which will [b]not change[/b]:[/p][list][*][p]The Art [i](which I am still wanting room for improvement for)[/i][/p][/*][*][p]The Weapons and Gunplay [i](these are the [b]corner stones [/b]of ProtonVR)[/i][/p][/*][*][p]The Setting, Lore and World-Building[/p][/*][/list][p]So what is going to change? [b]The genre.[/b][/p][p][/p][p][i]Note: Regarding the Art, it's Pixel Art and [b]there are not many games[/b] as successful with Pixel Art as Compound therefore, I'll concede that both games will always be visually [b]similar, [/b]that kind of feedback is Inevitable and completely acceptable![/i][/p][p][i]Remember when older FPS games were called [b]Doom-clones? [/b]Or [b]Wolf3D-clones[/b]?[/i][/p][h2]From [i]Roguelike[/i] to [b]Action Shooter[/b][/h2][p][/p][p]One of the things I cannot fail to mention, just by looking at the trailer, is that the gameplay [b]looks [/b]similar at a first glance to COMPOUND, why? The damn loop is too similar.
[/p][p][i]Open a door, shoot some enemies, open another door, shoot some more enemies in enclosed spaces, low ceilings and offices?![/i][/p][p][/p][p][b]The players are always right.[/b] And this is why I am [b]getting rid of all that[/b] and going for something completely different, something that was [b]planned [/b]is now going to come onto the [b]spotlight[/b].[/p][p]That's why ProtonVR [b]will no longer be considered a [i]Roguelike[/i] and will become an Action Shooter.[/b][/p][p][/p][h2]The Arena and Game Modes[/h2][p]ProtonVR will pivot towards a [b]more broad[/b] genre: [b]Action Shooters[/b][/p][p]One the one hand, this gets rid of the [b]creative constraints[/b] that come in building a Roguelike only game, but also cements ProtonVR's identity as [b]not COMPOUND, [/b] because one is a Roguelike and the other is not.
And as I mentioned above, I will [b]beyond[/b] the gameplay feel of what you are accustomed to in an Arcade 3D Pixelart game, I want to [b]give the player more freedom[/b]. Let's take it step by step.[/p][p][/p][h3]The Arena Map(s)[/h3][p]These maps are [b]larger [/b]maps that have several [b]zones[/b] that will require the player to adapt the [b]gameplay [/b]style. Within these maps there will be [b]several game-modes and objectives:[/b][/p][list][*][p]Hunting Targets[/p][/*][*][p]Extraction[/p][/*][*][p]Sabotage[/p][/*][*][p]Incursion[/p][/*][*][p]Seek and Destroy[/p][/*][*][p]Patrol[/p][/*][*][p]Capture and Defend[/p][/*][*][p]Timed Objectives[/p][/*][*][p]Wave Survival[/p][/*][/list][p]Movement will extend beyond just moving forwards and backwards, because some maps will have unique architectural features that will require the player to:[/p][list][*][p]Climb[/p][/*][*][p]Fly[/p][/*][*][p]Grapple[/p][/*][/list][p]This allows players to [b]really[/b] chose their own playstyle like I intended from the start.[/p][h3]What about [b]Procedurally Generated Levels?[/b][/h3][p]If you purchased the game because you like clearing rooms [b]fear not[/b]. That will still remain in the core of the game, but as a [b]game-mode on its own[/b] that complements the other many game modes.[/p][p]The reason while I am keeping this is that I want to encourage [b]play [/b]and [b]experimentation[/b], and for that I need two ingredients:[/p][list][*][p]A worthy Arsenal[/p][/*][*][p]Several scenarios, challenges and game-modes.[/p][/*][/list][p]The reason while I'm not calling ProtonVR an [i]Arena Shooter[/i] is that [b]I do not want to constrain myself to one game-mode[/b].[/p][p][/p][p][i]Thank your for reading through this, it's a big one.[/i][/p][p]-Sam[/p][p][/p][h3][i]TLDR:[/i][/h3][p]ProtonVR is pivoting from a roguelike to a broader VR action shooter with large arena maps, multiple objectives, vertical mobility (climbing, grappling, flying), and more...[/p][p]Procedural room-clearing [i](roguelike style)[/i] will remain as a separate mode, but the core loop will now focus on varied, open environments and dynamic objectives to create a gameplay identity distinct from COMPOUND.[/p]

notes.title: Trailer Released! Now what's next?
notes.notes:
[p]Hello all![/p][p][/p][p]That's was a fun edit! I hope this sparked some intrigue in you! Yes, [b]you![/b] 

I want to reach out to all who want to [b]actively participate[/b] in the [b]development[/b] of ProtonVR, the early stages of a game are very important to know, as a developer, if I am moving in the right direction with all gameplay features, difficulty, progression and overall combat.[/p][p][/p][p]But without a strong, united community this is impossible, but I am also excited to share with you the amazing things I can build to make this game of [b]ours[/b] (believe it or not I also love the game I am making), truly awesome.  

How can you help you ask?[/p][p]Simple: [b]Join the Discord[/b] and say hello![/p][p][url="https://discord.gg/A9JB4N65dc"]Discord Invite Link[/url][/p][p][/p][p]For now, baby steps. But in the near future I want to [b]maximize [/b]development transparency with the following:[/p][list][*][p]Making the [b]Trello[/b] board public[/p][/*][*][p]Regular weekly Dev Blogs news around Steam's Announcements (like this one)[/p][/*][/list][p][/p][p]More to follow![/p][p][/p][p]-Sam[/p]

notes.title: Demo Coming Soon
notes.notes:
[h1]Greetings![/h1]

Hello to all who are starting to join in on the community, and welcome!

Before I introduce myself I wish to express to those who have wishlisted ProtonVR my gratitude, is it humbling to know how many of you are interested in this game.

My name is Sam, I'm the sole developer of ProtonVR. Nice to meet you!

Lets get down to business, the [b]demo is releasing soon[/b]! It's pretty much in the pipeline for review and release by Steam's staff and before it comes out I wish to manage expectations and convey transparency regarding my intentions with this demo, so here's what you will find regarding content.

[h2]Demo Content[/h2]

[h3]Gameplay:[/h3]
[olist]
[*] Test and customize weapons in Armory.
[*] Rough UX for Inventory and Quick-Slots.
[*] Fight enemies in a procedurally generated level.
[*] Kill 10 enemies to return to the Armory.
[/olist]
[h3]Weapons:[/h3]
[list]
[*] Pistol
[*] Assault Rifle
[*] Bolt-Action Rifle
[*] Laser Rifle
[*] Plasma Rifle
[/list]
[h3]Attachments:[/h3]
[list]
[*] Four Scopes
[*] Two Holographic Sights
[*] One Laser
[/list]
[h3]Levels:[/h3]
[list]
[*] Armory
[*] Generated Level One (codename 'Engineering')
[/list]
[h3]Enemies:[/h3]
[list]
[*] Cyborg Grunt
[*] Firefly Drone
[/list]

[u]This demo will [b]never [/b]be time-limited[/u].
[h2]Goals[/h2]
This demo will help you track and influence the development progress of ProtonVR and, eventually, in it's more matured stage, when a release is available, is going to help players decide if they wish to purchase the game.

As you can see there is not a substantial amount of content yet in the demo, this is because the demo and the game will be developed in parallel, meaning that the demo will be continuously updated with most up-to-date systems while keeping weapons, enemies and level to a capped number respective to MVP-sized game.

This is so [b]players [/b]know exactly what kind of a state the game is and most importantly can [b]provide crucial feedback[/b] for its development.

For this feedback I recommend [b]joining the discord[/b] and feel free to say hello!
Will give more info when the demo is out and until then

[h3]Happy New Year!!![/h3]

-Sam
